_doc: Shared summary cases: worker.py (tests/test_parity.py) and the hub (meetings_minutes_test.go) must both produce every 'want'. The inputs are hand-written and made up; the wants come from worker.py: regenerate them with QUORUM_UPDATE_CASES=1 pytest tests/test_parity.py, then make the Go side pass.

wantMergePrompt.content:
You merge the minutes of consecutive parts of one meeting into the minutes of the whole meeting. Answer with only one JSON object of this shape:
{"title": string, "summary": string (3 to 5 lines), "topics": [string], "decisions": [{"text": string, "ts": "mm:ss"}], "openPoints": [{"text": string, "ts": "mm:ss"}], "actions": [{"text": string, "owner": string, "due": string, "ts": "mm:ss"}], "attendees": [string]}
Rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. The transcript is automatic and may contain errors.
- Never invent owners or due dates: if the transcript does not say who does an action or by when, use "".
- A decision is something the participants agreed on; an open point is something left unresolved.
- Cite the transcript timestamp ("mm:ss") where each decision, open point and action was said.
- Attendees are the names of people that appear in the transcript; never list generic labels like "Speaker 2".
- Write every text in Spanish.
- Keep every decision, open point and action of the parts (merge exact duplicates), with their owners, due dates and timestamps unchanged. An open point that a later part resolved becomes a decision.
- The summary covers the whole meeting in 3 to 5 lines.
